_meta.purpose: Hard filters. These reject a posting before scoring, and every rejection writes a `rejection` row naming the rule and quoting the evidence that fired it.
_meta.reversibility: Rejections are stored, never deleted, and the posting keeps its row. Disable a rule here and re-run to get those postings back.
split_from_eligibility: A hard filter answers a question about the POSTING: is it a real, current, professional vacancy in a place the user will consider.
Eligibility (T037) answers a question about the READER: may this person hold this role, given their own confirmed citizenship, qualifications and languages.

The legacy config mixed the two, and every profile-dependent rule in it was written against one candidate — 'candidate_languages: english, urdu, punjabi' and 'citizenship: PK only' were literals in the filter table. Those rules moved to eligibility, where they are read from the user's own profile records, and where a wrong answer SOFT-HIDES with a reason instead of rejecting: a profile fact can be missing, stale or simply unconfirmed, and the fix is to correct the profile rather than to re-crawl a board.
_meta.logging_rule: Every rejection names the exact rule and the evidence string that triggered it. A rejected posting is never silently dropped.

filters.label: Posting lacks a title, employer or source URL
filters.rationale: A record that cannot be traced to a source URL cannot be part of an auditable system, and a posting with no title or employer cannot be applied to.

filters.label: Posting is an internship, apprenticeship, working-student or volunteer role
filters.rationale: A user with documented professional experience is looking for professional-level work. This is about the posting's level, not about the reader.
filters.applies_to_rationale: Matched against the title alone. These words appear routinely in the body of ordinary descriptions ('you will mentor interns'), and matching there rejects good roles.

filters.label: Posting is older than the staleness window
filters.window_setting_rationale: The window is the `staleness_window_days` setting, not a number here, so one value governs both what discovery re-fetches and what scoring rejects. Two windows for one idea drift apart.
filters.null_date_rationale: A posting with no date is NOT rejected. Rejecting on a missing value treats an unknown as a fact, and several sources simply do not publish a date.

filters.label: Posting requires substantially more experience than the user has documented
filters.rationale: A stated year requirement is often aspirational, so the threshold is deliberately generous: only a demand more than six years above what the user can document rejects. Experience is also a scored component, so a smaller gap is reflected in the score rather than in an exclusion.
filters.unknown_years_rationale: A user whose documented years cannot be established is not filtered on them. Comparing a requirement against an unknown would reject the whole board for an unfinished profile.

filters.label: Posting is in a country the user has excluded
filters.rationale: EMPTY BY DESIGN. Which countries are searched at all is the `country` table's `enabled` flag (T031 country packs); this rule exists for a place a user will not go to even though the pack is on. Country preference as a ranking bonus lives in country_preferences.json, not here.

filters.label: MOVED — posting refuses visa sponsorship outside the user's own country
filters.rationale: Depends on the reader's citizenship and residence, so it is an eligibility question and soft-hides with a reason. Enabling it here would reject on a profile fact that may be unconfirmed.

filters.label: MOVED — posting requires a national security clearance
filters.rationale: A clearance requires citizenship of the issuing country, so whether it excludes the reader depends on the reader.

filters.label: MOVED — posting requires citizenship or settled status
filters.rationale: Same reason as F01. The demand is detected at ingest and compared against the user's own confirmed citizenship.

filters.label: MOVED — posting requires a qualification above the user's
filters.rationale: Compared against the user's own documented highest qualification on the configured ladder. A Master's requirement does not exclude a Master's holder, and the legacy rule could only encode one candidate's degree.

filters.label: MOVED — posting requires a language the user has not confirmed
filters.rationale: The legacy rule listed one candidate's three languages as literals. Eligibility reads the user's own confirmed `languages[].language` records, and a demand whose language could not be read is UNSCORED rather than treated as satisfied.
